transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-12-01 08:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Redwood CSM); Dr. Maya Thompson, Ethan Park, Sofia Alvarez, Omar Khan, Leah Brooks (Synthesis Health)

Summary: Quick kickoff for onboarding Synthesis Health onto Redwood. Covering access, security requirements (SSO, KMS), target piloting plan, responsibilities and timeline, and next technical deep-dive scheduling.

00:00 Alex Rivera: morning everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is the kickoff for the Synthesis Health onboarding with Redwood, I'm Alex Rivera, I'll be your AE and Marcus is your CSM, Priya is our SE, uh quick roundtable?
00:14 Dr. Maya Thompson: hi all, Maya here, head of data at Synthesis, excited to get started, we're mostly focused on embedding-powered search and some triage chat flows for clinical support
00:27 Ethan Park: Ethan, eng manager, we'll own integrations, infra side is Leah, security is Sofia
00:34 Alex Rivera: awesome, thanks. Priya, you want to run the agenda?
00:39 Priya Nair: sure, quick agenda — onboarding timeline, access & infra (VPC, peering), security & compliance (SAML, KMS, audit logs), pilot plan and success criteria, wrap and next steps
00:58 Priya Nair: so first access: we'll need an admin user for the console, and service account keys for test env, we support both hosted api and private deployments, you mentioned you want private, is that still right Maya?
01:12 Dr. Maya Thompson: yes, given PHI concerns we want private deployment in our VPC, ideally customer-managed keys, and audit logs stored in our logging cluster
01:27 Sofia Alvarez: also SOC 2 and ISO reqs — do you have the attestation and the SOC 2 report? We need it for the vendor review
01:35 Alex Rivera: yes we can share our SOC 2 report and our standard security pack, I'll drop links after call. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and HSM integrations, we also have options for on-prem HSM if needed
01:50 Sofia Alvarez: great, please include details on key rotation and separation of duties
01:55 Priya Nair: note on private mode — we deploy a private control plane which talks to your VPC via peered endpoints, networking teams often want to allow specific egress and CIDR blocks, we'll share the required ports and ip ranges
02:13 Leah Brooks: on that, do we need AWS Transit Gateway or just VPC peering?
02:18 Priya Nair: we typically support direct VPC peering, transit gateway is also fine if that's your standard, there are some differences in routing for multi-region deployments
02:32 Marcus Li: quick addition — for Dedicated vs Private: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools managed by Redwood, Private is the VPC-hosted control plane with customer-managed infra; sounds like Private is the fit here
02:45 Omar Khan: to confirm, models stay inside our VPC? Any egress to public internet?
02:50 Priya Nair: models execute on infra that you control, but management/control plane may need outbound to our control plane unless you choose the fully on-prem package; we'll clarify the exact traffic flows in the network doc
03:10 Ethan Park: performance-wise we plan to run a pilot with 50 concurrent users, are there throughput numbers we should expect?
03:20 Priya Nair: yes for a pilot we can size a small cluster — recommend starting with 2 GPU instances for inference, we can provide our throughput guidance; note that batching and KV cache can improve per-token cost but adds latency tradeoffs, we'll tune based on your latency SLOs
03:40 Dr. Maya Thompson: what's your typical p99 latency for chat flows?
03:48 Priya Nair: depending on model and sequence length, p99 can be 150-400ms for optimized models on our runtime, but in private deployments network latency should be accounted for, so we can run benchmarks during the pilot
04:05 Alex Rivera: we'll add a benchmarking run as part of the pilot, SE to own setup and results
04:11 Priya Nair: yep I'll run the initial benchmarks and share the sheets. we'll also demo our model pinning and rollout controls so you can canary new model versions
04:26 Sofia Alvarez: on compliance — audit logs, retention, and RBAC are critical, can you export logs to our SIEM?
04:34 Priya Nair: we can stream audit logs to your S3 bucket or SIEM via Kinesis/CloudWatch logs, and RBAC integrates with SAML groups for role mapping
04:48 Sofia Alvarez: okay, please include the mapping doc, and the minimum permissions we need for the service account
04:55 Alex Rivera: noted, I'll send the role mapping template. Marcus, did you want to cover onboarding milestones and timeline?
05:03 Marcus Li: sure, typical onboarding — week 0: access & infra setup, week 1: private deployment provisioning + SSO, week 2: pilot run with benchmark, week 3: evaluation and tuning, week 4: production cutover planning — we can compress or expand based on your readiness
05:28 Ethan Park: that timeline works for us, we aim to pilot by mid-December, ideally 12/15 for pilot start
05:35 Marcus Li: ok that aligns, we'll prioritize SSO and networking this week
05:40 Dr. Maya Thompson: stakeholders for go/no-go will be security and product, and exec sign-off after pilot metrics look good
05:51 Priya Nair: question: do you have any data residency needs across regions?
05:56 Dr. Maya Thompson: US only for now, but may expand to EU next year
06:03 Priya Nair: great we'll note that in the deployment config.
06:12 Alex Rivera: any blockers on legal or procurement?
06:16 Omar Khan: procurement is reviewing, should be quick but need SOC 2 and standard contract redlines, procurement team will follow up with Marcus
06:26 Marcus Li: I'll coordinate with procurement, share the SOW and contract templates after the call
06:35 Leah Brooks: network question — do you provide terraform modules or IaC for the VPC peering and infra?
06:42 Priya Nair: yes we have terraform modules and CloudFormation examples, we'll share those in the runbook repo, plus a quickstart script for the initial env
06:55 Ethan Park: for the pilot we'll want a small integration point — likely via Redwood API for embeddings and a Webhook for chat events; are there SDKs?
07:03 Priya Nair: yes SDKs in Python/Node and REST endpoints, we'll share code samples for embeddings and streaming chat, there might be minor name mismatches in docs but we'll point you to the latest repo
07:20 Dr. Maya Thompson: curious on cost controls — can we set per-route quotas and alarms?
07:25 Marcus Li: yes, Redwood Console has token-level cost breakdowns and per-route quota enforcement, you can set alerts and throttle for budget control
07:36 Sofia Alvarez: are there encryption-in-transit details? TLS mutual auth?
07:40 Priya Nair: all traffic is TLS 1.2+, and for private peering we can support mTLS for service-to-service if you require it, we'll document cert rotation and keys
07:54 Alex Rivera: quick note we also support model quantization recommendations if you want to reduce cost while keeping quality, Redwood Optimize has suggestions but SE will help tune profiles
08:10 Priya Nair: right, and we can run evals against your prompts to ensure model quality before cutover
08:20 Ethan Park: ok good. what about escalation and support SLAs?
08:24 Marcus Li: enterprise plans include 24/7 incident support and a defined SLA, and we can configure on-call flows with your ops team, I'll send the SLA details
08:36 Omar Khan: for pilot success criteria — we'll define latency p95/p99 targets, accuracy on sample prompts, and cost per 1k tokens. Maya will confirm thresholds after this call
08:50 Dr. Maya Thompson: I'll follow up with the concrete thresholds by EOD Friday
08:56 Priya Nair: perfect. any blockers for initial access?
09:00 Leah Brooks: we'll need the admin console invite and a service account key for the test env; also will open a ticket for IP allowlist changes
09:10 Alex Rivera: I'll send invites today and open the onboarding ticket, include the runbook link, security doc and the terraform modules
09:20 Priya Nair: last thing — network diagram and required ports will be in the runbook, look for that in the onboarding bucket
09:34 Marcus Li: recap of next steps: Alex sends docs and invites, Priya schedules deep-dive, Sofia sends SAML metadata, Leah provides test data, Ethan provides success criteria, Marcus will share contract/SOW with procurement
09:50 Dr. Maya Thompson: sounds good, thanks everyone, excited to get started
09:55 Alex Rivera: thanks all, we'll follow up with the items in the next 48 hours
10:00 Meeting end

Notes: transcript has minor transcription artifacts (names sometimes spelled differently, a couple of dropped words). Links mentioned during the call: onboarding runbook (link to be sent), SOC 2 report (link to be sent), terraform modules repo (link to be sent).

End of transcript.
